Subject: SRH RFP — follow-up: commercial clarifications

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the RFP materials — we've reviewed the technical answers and have a concentrated set of commercial questions so our procurement team can compare apples-to-apples across vendors. Could you please clarify the following and return a concise commercial summary? We need this by EOD PT on Monday to keep the approval cadence.

1) Committed volumes and unit definition: confirm pricing per 1M tokens and how a "token" is measured for mixed chat/generation workloads.
2) Overage treatment: unit price for usage above commit and whether overage is flat or tiered.
3) Burst smoothing / cushion: do you provide a monthly burst allowance (credits) and how is it applied?
4) True-up cadence & invoicing: monthly vs. quarterly true-up; net terms; any prepay/discount options.
5) Model-specific adders: different pricing for high-capacity models (e.g., 70B family) vs baseline open models.
6) SLA crediting and refund mechanics tied to latency/availability.
7) Pilot pricing for a one-month evaluation (expected ~8M tokens).

I've attached the RFP appendix for pricing (Attachment-A). If useful, we can carve a 30-minute call first thing Monday.

Appreciate the fast turnaround —
Sara
Sara Kim
Director, Procurement
SunRidge Health

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Hi Sara — thanks, and we can absolutely get this to you quickly. Below is a concise commercial summary aligned to the points in your note. I've attached a formal offer and an editable pricing model for your finance team.

Executive summary (concise)
- Committed tiers priced per 1,000,000 (1M) tokens. Tokens measured using Redwood's standard tokenization for mixed chat/generation (byte-pair encoding; we normalize on 1M-token units in invoices).
- Overage is charged on a per-1M basis and is tiered (see table). Smoothing: monthly burst credits are applied before overage billing.
- True-up cadence: monthly measurement with quarterly invoicing reconciliation (default); option for monthly invoicing on request.
- Model adders: separate pricing bands for large-parameter families; adder expressed as % of base unit price.
- Pilot: one-month pilot offer available at 50% of the committed Silver rate (details below).

Commercial table (high level)
- Bronze: 10M tokens/month committed — $18 per 1M tokens — burst cushion: 5% (1.0M tokens)
- Silver: 30M tokens/month committed — $15 per 1M tokens — burst cushion: 10% (3.0M tokens)
- Gold: 100M tokens/month committed — $12 per 1M tokens — burst cushion: 20% (20.0M tokens)

Overage (usage above monthly commit + cushion)
- Tiered overage: 0–20% overage: 1.15x committed unit price; 20–50% overage: 1.35x; >50% overage: 1.6x. Overage measured per calendar month after applied burst cushion.

Smoothing / burst credit mechanics
- Monthly burst cushion applies automatically (as stated above). Any usage consumed within cushion is free relative to committed unit price. If usage exceeds commit + cushion, overage pricing applies.
- We offer a 3-month rolling smoothing option (optional add-on) where we average usage across three months for billing to reduce peak impact; this requires annual commit and enrollment at contract signature.

True-up, invoicing, and payment terms
- Default: monthly usage measurement + quarterly invoice reconciliation (true-up). Standard net-30 payment terms.
- Prepay discounts: pay-annual-upfront — 5% discount on listed unit prices; 2-year upfront — 10% discount.

Model-specific pricing
- Baseline open models (Redwood-open-13B-like): base unit price as above.
- Large models (70B+ families): 35% adder over base unit price. Customized model bundles can be negotiated; per-request cost ceilings provided for planning.

SLA crediting
- Availability SLA: 99.9% on provisioned Dedicated pools; credits capped at 20% of monthly invoice for qualifying events. Latency SLOs are documented in the SLA addendum; credits issued as invoice adjustments.

Pilot offering
- One-month pilot (approx 8M tokens) can be executed at 50% of Silver committed rate ($7.5 per 1M tokens) with no long-term obligation. Pilot includes basic observability; production-grade SLA requires contract execution.

Next steps
- If this structure looks acceptable, we'll provide a contract-ready quote and the redlined commercial appendix. Ben has attached the pricing model so your FP&A can simulate scenarios.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Jordan — thanks for the clean summary. A couple of suggested edits before we send the formal PDF to SunRidge:

1) Overage multipliers: drop the 0–20% overage multiplier to 1.12x (from 1.15x) to be more competitive; keep the higher bands as-is.
2) Payment terms: SunRidge is a health system — consider offering Net-45 for the first year or Net-60 with a small admin fee; check with finance.
3) Pilot: make pilot explicitly refundable toward first committed month if they convert within 30 days — reduces friction.

Ben: please refresh the model with the adjusted multiplier and an annual prepay 6% discount scenario so we can show impact to list price. Jordan: once Ben provides the updated spreadsheet I'll generate the quote PDF.

-Marissa
VP, Commercial
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SRH RFP — commercial terms & burst protection (initial offer)

Looping in the refreshed numbers (summary below). I updated the attached spreadsheet with scenarios (monthly/quarterly true-up, Net-30/45/60, and prepay sensitivity). Key takeaways:

- Moving 0–20% overage multiplier from 1.15x to 1.12x reduces expected overage revenue by ~2.4% in our mid-case but materially improves competitive score vs. two peers.
- Net-45 increases DSO but keeps win probability higher for large health systems; recommend Net-45 with a 1.0% administration fee if finance won't accept Net-60.
- Pilot refundable credit: modeling shows converting clients recover pilot cost within first committed month for Silver and Gold tiers.

I've attached redwood-pricing-model-v3.xlsx with scenario tabs. Recommend we send the updated commercial offer with Marissa's language edits and include a short annex on true-up examples.

-Ben
Senior Pricing Analyst
Redwood Inference
